what_it_measures: Online grocery orders from ONE chain: fall in that chain's own in-store spend per online dollar
number: under 0.40 USD per online dollar (own chain; a snippet of another version says 0.45, unverified)
unit_matches_sigma: Partly: it is the chain's own cannibalisation only; dollars taken from rival stores also count as avoided in-store spend
review_note: Do not call 0.40 a ceiling. Economy-wide in-store displacement for groceries is at least this, and plausibly more. Grocery only, one chain.

study: Chava, Oettl, Singh, Zeng (2022) NBER WP 30077
what_it_measures: Average nearby store sales after a fulfilment centre opens
number: -4% of store sales; exit probability +3 percentage points
unit_matches_sigma: No: a percent of store sales, not dollars per online dollar. Converting needs the local rise in online spend, which is not available here
review_note: Cannot be used as a low anchor for sigma in these units. Shows real store-level substitution near Amazon-type fulfilment centres.

what_it_measures: Trips of online-grocery adopters (JPMorgan Chase Institute card data)
number: -7.4% grocery-store trips (6.8 to 6.3 per month); +12.3% local ground transport spend; more trips to coffee shops, restaurants, personal care, leisure, pharmacies
unit_matches_sigma: No: trips, not dollars. It informs the trip offset: the replaced store trip falls, other trips rise
review_note: Trips fall less than one-for-one; grocery only; not Amazon-specific.

what_it_measures: Visa spend: convenience gain from online vs offline merchants
number: convenience gain at most 0.4% of consumption; most gain is variety; online share about 5% (2007) to 8% (2017)
review_note: Context for how much online spending is new variety rather than substitution.
